report:
## Conclusion

The claim is **accurate**. Kyleena, a low-dose levonorgestrel-releasing intrauterine system (19.5 mg, releasing ~17.5 mcg/day initially), was approved by the U.S. FDA in September 2016 specifically for the prevention of pregnancy for up to five years. This is confirmed in Bayer's official FDA approval announcement and the drug's full prescribing information, which states plainly under "Indications and Usage": "Kyleena is indicated to prevent pregnancy for up to 5 years."

Clinical trial data supporting this approval come from a Phase III study of 1,452 women aged 18–35 (both parous and nulliparous). The Pearl Index (a measure of contraceptive failures per 100 woman-years) was 0.16 in year one and rose to 0.29 cumulatively after five years, corresponding to a cumulative five-year pregnancy rate of about 1.45% (Kaplan-Meier estimate). This indicates the device remains more than 99% effective per year of use throughout the approved five-year duration, and the device must be removed or replaced after five years, as it is not approved for use beyond that period.

**Sources:**
- Bayer/PR Newswire, FDA approval announcement: https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/fda-approves-bayers-kyleena-levonorgestrel-releasing-intrauterine-system-195-mg-for-prevention-of-pregnancy-for-up-to-five-years-300330006.html
- Drugs.com prescribing information: https://www.drugs.com/pro/kyleena.html
- Bayer official Kyleena prescribing information (PI): https://www.bayer.com/sites/default/files/KYLEENA_EN_PI.pdf
- Kyleena HCP efficacy page: https://www.kyleenahcp.com/about-kyleena/efficacy
